findings.claim: The pass-1 guard `if: ${{ !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'changeset-release/') }}` keyed the exemption on a value the PR author chooses: any PR from a branch named `changeset-release/<anything>` (GitHub's startsWith is case-insensitive) skipped the hard floor, and a fork's head_ref is the bare branch name, so a fork could name it too.
findings.counterexample: Open a PR to main from branch `changeset-release/tweak` touching doctrine/** with no deposit: the step is skipped, `Totem Lint` is green, ruleset `main-required-checks` is satisfied. FOLDED (f8a1a109): a job-level `LEGS_GATE_RELEASE_TRAIN` predicate — exact name `changeset-release/main` AND `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository` — defined once and read by the notice step (== 'true') and the gate step (!= 'true').

findings.claim: The parity test that keeps the gate step hard asserted only `not.toContain('continue-on-error')` and `not.toContain('--depth=1')` on the step slice, so any `if:` on the step — a prefix match, `if: false`, an author-controlled value — passed the suite while softening the floor.
findings.counterexample: Replace the guard with `if: false`: the full suite still passes. FOLDED (f8a1a109): `readLintWorkflow()` / `gateStepOf()` helpers and a new test that asserts the exact env definition, exactly one `if:` on the gate step equal to the predicate's negation, no `startsWith(`, the notice step preceding the gate on the same predicate, and the notice title. The new test fails on both the pre-fold workflow and main's (no env definition, a different or absent `if:`).

findings.claim: The skip was silent, against this file's own never-skip-silently posture (the advisory annotation step exists for exactly that): a green `Totem Lint` on a release-train PR was indistinguishable from one where the floor ran.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (f8a1a109): a `release-train notice` step gated on the same predicate echoes `::notice title=totem legs gate SKIPPED::…` before the gate step.

findings.claim: The Reach disclosure said the CI arm is totem's enforcement without naming the one branch now outside it; `docs/wiki/**` is itself an owed glob.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (f8a1a109): one sentence appended to the Reach bullet naming the release train (same repository, exact name), the notice, and that `totem lint` still runs there (mmnto-ai/totem#2779).

findings.claim: The fold made this PR legs-owed (docs/wiki/**) and it carried no deposit: its own gate step reds `Totem Lint` (observed: run 33952349797, exit 3, head 25981722 = the merge ref of f8a1a109).
findings.counterexample: ANSWERED by this deposit, keyed to f8a1a109 (the head pass 2 read); the pass-2 fold and the deposit commit follow it as descendants.

findings.claim: The comment's rationale for the exact-name half was false at source: GitHub compares strings case-insensitively for `==` and `startsWith` alike (expressions reference), so case-insensitivity does not distinguish the exact test from the prefix test; only prefix-widening does.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (pass-2 fold): the job-env comment and the test comment say `==` and `startsWith` are both case-insensitive and that case is not the distinction.

findings.claim: The env-predicate assertion read the whole workflow text, comments included: a `#` decoy carrying the exact string above a prefix predicate passed the new test (constructed and verified by the leg).
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: `lintJobHeaderOf()` slices the `lint` job header to its `steps:` key with comment lines dropped (shared `dropComments`), and the assertion reads that slice.

findings.claim: A residual skip path remains: a writer with push access to this repository who names a branch exactly `changeset-release/main` (any case) skips the hard step; the comment implied closure.
findings.counterexample: DISCLOSED in the job-env comment as the residual, with its trust boundary (the same trust that lets that writer merge). Not closed: a title or actor predicate is author-controlled too (the VP-PR's author is the PAT owner, the same identity as human seats).

findings.claim: The comment said `changeset-release/<base>` is the action's default; at the pinned SHA it is `changeset-release/${github.ref_name}` of the RELEASE workflow's push (main), which coincides with the PR base here.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: the comment now reads `changeset-release/<ref_name of that push>`, so `changeset-release/main` here.

findings.claim: The 38-line HARD-gate comment block sat above the notice step and read as that step's leading comment.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: the release-train paragraph sits above the notice step; the HARD-gate block sits directly above the gate step, with one added clause naming the release train as its only skip.

findings.claim: Pass 3 (on 5b271cb5, the shape-check fold that answered Greptile's P1): an M-only CHANGELOG arm judges a legitimate Version Packages diff out of shape — a new package's first release ADDS its CHANGELOG (PR mmnto-ai/totem#2514 in history), so the next cut that adds a package would red exactly as mmnto-ai/totem#2778 did.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): the CHANGELOG arm admits A and M; executed over VP + `A packages/newpkg/CHANGELOG.md` → exempt.

findings.claim: The comment claimed a diff that cannot be derived fails the step, but the step had no `shell: bash` and so no pipefail: a failed `git diff` piped into the filter yielded an empty list, `exempt=true`, gate skipped — fail-open.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): `shell: bash` plus `set -euo pipefail`, the diff captured in its own assignment before filtering; a failed diff in a fresh bash process exits 128 before the next line (executed).

findings.claim: The test asserted the presence of both `exempt=` writes and both annotations but not which branch writes which: swapping the branches passed every assertion while the gate would then be skipped exactly when the diff is out of shape.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): `runLinesOf()` pins the check step's run block exactly, in order.

findings.claim: awk's default field splitting exempted `M sub/CHANGELOG.md more` (a whitespace-carrying path), so an owed path named with a space could be exempted.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): whole-line anchored grep -E patterns; executed: `M sub/CHANGELOG.md more` and `M doctrine/package.json rules.md` are kept.

findings.claim: `D .changeset/README.md` matched the deleted-changeset pattern and was exempted; the action never deletes it and it is an owed path.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239, re-folded in the post-convergence commit): a README-deletion line is appended to the out-of-shape list; executed: kept, including under a 560 KB diff.

findings.claim: The `::warning` interpolated a multi-line list; only the first line lands in the annotation.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): the list is flattened to one line with `paste`.

findings.claim: `stepNamed` located the step before dropping comments, so a `#` line carrying `- name: release-train check` earlier in the file could anchor the slice.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (963e7239): comments are dropped first in `stepNamed` and `lintJobHeaderOf`.

findings.claim: Pass 4 (on 963e7239): the README guard used `echo "$diff" | grep -q` under pipefail; once the diff exceeds the pipe buffer, grep -q exits on the match, echo takes SIGPIPE, the pipeline reads 141 and the condition false — the README deletion is dropped as in-shape (measured at 20,000 lines; latent, the largest VP diff has 16).
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (post-convergence commit): a `grep -E` that consumes its whole input captures README lines into a variable appended to the list; executed at 560,023 bytes: kept.

findings.claim: The comment quantified the shape over 60 Version Packages PRs; the population selected by the predicate is 259 by head ref (2,646 file entries, statuses A/D/M only, zero out of shape — the leg's census).
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: the comment names the leg's census and this seat's own read (252 PRs, 2,572 entries, the same).

findings.claim: 'never an empty list read as in shape' overstated: an EMPTY diff is exempt (the failed derivation is what aborts).
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: the comment says a failing fetch or diff aborts and an empty diff is exempt, as the gate itself would derive not-owed.

findings.claim: The package.json arm admitted six tracked paths the action never writes (services/, spikes/, examples/, two fixtures, the private root package.json).
findings.counterexample: FOLDED: both arms narrow to `packages/<one segment>/` (the workspace glob); a census of every merged VP-PR from the release branch shows every CHANGELOG and package.json path under it; executed: the six paths and the root CHANGELOG are kept.

findings.claim: Between pass 4 and pass 5, Greptile's follow-up on the PR showed shape is not provenance: a same-repository push to the release branch deleting ONE pending changeset and nothing else satisfied the shape and was exempted — a writer could drop a pending changeset silently.
findings.counterexample: FOLDED (d97023b7): the check moved into tools/release-train-shape.sh, which also requires the deleted changesets to equal the pending set (no subset, never README) and a rendered CHANGELOG whenever changesets were consumed; the subset-deletion case is executed in release-train-shape.test.ts and is not exempt; the annotation is static with reasons in the log.

findings.claim: Pass 5 (on d97023b7, the head this deposit is keyed to): the narration overclaimed 'EXACTLY the train's work' — with nothing pending, rewritten CHANGELOG/package.json content was exempt (executed: `# TOTALLY FABRICATED` + a postinstall). No floor lost: neither path is an owed glob, so the gate derives not-owed on that diff anyway; a release-integrity concern for the cut sensor.

findings.claim: Assertion strength: no exempt-side case covered the pending-empty class, and four not-exempt cases asserted only the outcome, so each could pass for the wrong rule.

findings.counterexample: FOLDED: `--no-renames`; the first-release case reuses the deleted changeset's text verbatim for the added CHANGELOG and stays exempt (executed).

verdict: Pass 1 (origin/main...bcfc26b5): no BLOCKING; F1 and F2 MATERIAL, F3 and F4 MINOR; the five assertions of the diff held under attack (head_ref always set on pull_request-only triggers and fail-closed if a trigger is added; changeset-release/<ref_name> is changesets/action's default at the pinned SHA and release.yml passes no branch:; the skipped fetch is not load-bearing, the lint step fetches for itself; a feature PR still fails; prepareBranch resets the version branch to the new main sha so the regenerated VP-PR re-runs under the amended workflow); `Totem Lint` is the only red check on mmnto-ai/totem#2778 and it turned red exactly at the gate's introduction. Convergence NOT named on pass 1. Pass 2, re-armed on the fold (bcfc26b5..f8a1a109): no BLOCKING; pass-1 F1–F4 all CLOSED; the Actions semantics verified against primary docs (env available in step if:, github in job env, boolean casts to exactly 'true'/'false', null degrades fail-closed, a fork's head.repo.full_name is the fork so the gate runs, the new test fails on both prior workflows: 6 and 5 assertions); seven items, two MATERIAL (the missing deposit; a false case-insensitivity rationale), the rest text and test scoping — six folded, one disclosed as a residual (p2-f4). Pass 2 named convergence, but its disclosed residual (a repo writer pushing owed changes onto the release branch) was named reachable by Greptile's P1 and answered by a mechanism: the release train is identified by its diff SHAPE (5b271cb5), so the leg re-armed. Pass 3 (5b271cb5..): no BLOCKING; three MATERIAL (an ADDED CHANGELOG in history, mmnto-ai/totem#2514; fail-open without pipefail; the branch order unpinned) and five MINOR, all folded (963e7239); convergence NOT named. Pass 4 (963e7239, the head this deposit is keyed to): no BLOCKING; CONVERGENCE NAMED on the CI mechanism, the shape validated against the full population of release-branch VP-PRs (259 by head ref, 2,646 file entries, zero out of shape); one latent MATERIAL (grep -q SIGPIPE under pipefail, unreachable at today's diff sizes) and three accuracy items, folded in the post-convergence commit with executed probes in a fresh bash process (real VP diff exempt; ADDED CHANGELOG exempt; deleted README kept, including at 560 KB; non-workspace and root package.json/CHANGELOG kept; whitespace path kept; empty diff exempt; failed diff aborts), no re-arm. Then Greptile's follow-up on the PR showed shape is not provenance (a subset deletion of pending changesets was exempt), answered by a mechanism in d97023b7 (tools/release-train-shape.sh: shape + the deleted set equals the pending set + a rendered CHANGELOG; 11 executed cases), so the leg re-armed. Pass 5 (d97023b7, the head this deposit is keyed to): no BLOCKING; CONVERGENCE NAMED; Greptile's follow-up CLOSED on both points; two MATERIAL (a narration overclaim on the nothing-pending class — no floor lost, the paths are not owed; assertion strength on four cases) and four MINOR, all folded in the post-convergence commit with executed cases (13 cases plus bash -n, 21 tests across the two files) and the script re-run against the real release branch (merge base b8fe7edd): exempt=true. No further re-arm: the refinements (merge-base pending, --no-renames, the nothing-pending rule) are covered by executed cases.
